title: "CAP Analysis Report 2023-2025: Quality Management Insights"
description: "Comprehensive analysis of Corrective Action Plans (CAP) including trends, costs, suppliers, and performance metrics"
author: "Pardus Agent"
date: "2025-02-17"

children.content: CAP Analysis Report 2023-2025: Quality Management Insights
This report provides a comprehensive analysis of 37 Corrective Action Plans

recorded between February 2023 and September 2025. The analysis reveals key trends, cost patterns, supplier performance, and closure efficiency metrics that can inform strategic quality management decisions.

content.content: : Claims account for 54% of all CAPs
: 75% of CAPs closed within 3 months, with average closure time of 82 days
: 2024 showed highest activity with 17 CAPs and €388,451 in costs

children.content: The CAP data spans from February 2023 to September 2025, covering 37 unique corrective action plans across multiple suppliers, customers, and quality issue types. All CAPs fall under the NVSA
category, indicating systematic quality management processes.

content.content: : Global customer base including China, Europe, and other regions

children.content: The CAP data reveals four primary types of quality issues:

Claims represent not only the most frequent CAP type but also the most costly, accounting for 71.6% of total expenditures. This suggests that customer-facing quality issues have significant financial implications and should be prioritized for preventive measures.
: Over half of all CAPs are claims-related, indicating strong customer quality assurance processes
show balanced attention to internal and external quality issues
: Despite being only 54% of total CAPs, claims represent 71.6% of total costs

root cause analysis provides insights into the underlying causes of CAPs:
: Nearly half of all CAPs stem from procedural or method-related problems
: 16.2% indicate systemic management or oversight issues

: Material issues require enhanced supplier quality management and incoming inspection
: Management-related CAPs indicate need for leadership training and accountability systems

children.content: Based on the comprehensive analysis, the following strategic recommendations are proposed:
: Address the 88.6% cost concentration in top 3 suppliers

content.content: Develop supplier quality agreements with Mitsubishi, Inopor, and Dupont
Implement incoming quality inspection for high-value equipment
Establish alternative sourcing strategies for critical components
Create joint quality improvement programs with key suppliers

children.content: : 50-70% reduction in high-cost CAPs within 12-18 months
: Address 46% of CAPs caused by method-related issues

content.content: Review and update Standard Operating Procedures
Enhance training programs for installation and commissioning teams
Implement process validation and verification protocols
Create checklists and quality control points for critical steps

children.content: : 30-40% reduction in method-related CAPs within 6-12 months

content.content: Implement CAP complexity scoring for more accurate closure date estimation
Establish CAP management team with dedicated resources
Create CAP tracking dashboard with automated alerts
Standardize CAP documentation and approval processes

children.content: : Improve closure time consistency, reduce average to 60-70 days
: Reduce overall CAP volume by addressing root causes

content.content: Develop CAP trend analysis and early warning system
Implement preventive maintenance programs for high-risk equipment
Create customer-specific risk profiles and mitigation plans
Establish lessons learned database and knowledge sharing platform

children.content: : 20-30% reduction in CAP volume over 2 years

content.content: Develop customer-specific installation and operation guidelines

children.content: The CAP analysis for 2023-2025 reveals a well-structured quality management system with strong closure performance
but significant opportunities for improvement in cost control and prevention.
: Tackle 46% of CAPs through process improvement
: Standardize CAP management for consistent results
: Move from reactive to proactive quality management

content.content: : €200,000-300,000 cost reduction through supplier quality improvements
: €400,000-500,000 cost reduction through method improvements and prevention
: €600,000+ total cost reduction with comprehensive quality management system

children.content: The data suggests that while the current CAP management system is effective in closing issues, there is significant opportunity to prevent CAPs before they occur, reduce their cost impact, and improve overall quality performance through strategic interventions focused on supplier quality, method improvement, and predictive quality management.

This analysis was conducted using Python with pandas and Plotly for data processing and visualization. Data was cleaned to remove null values and standardize date formats. All monetary values are presented in Euros
